subject: Draft MAP & evaluation plan for Fabricate pilot
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fabricate.ai>
Date: 2026-03-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MAP & evaluation plan for Fabricate pilot

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, I’m sharing a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) template and a lightweight evaluation plan to help align timelines and owners for the Fabricate pilot. Attached: MAP_Template_v1.docx and a short slide that summarizes the phase gates. I’ve also put a living copy in Google Docs so your team can comment inline: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X8mSAMPLE_MAP_DRAFT

Quick asks so we can get the MAP ready before the kickoff:
- Can you confirm target success criteria (e.g., intent accuracy >= 85%, end-to-end latency < 400ms p50, embeddings quality measures)?
- Who should be the Fabricate owners for data ingestion, security review, and procurement?
- Do you have any hard blackout dates or procurement windows in Q2?

Proposed high-level timeline (editable):
1) Discovery & scope alignment — Mar 22–Mar 31
2) Small-scale evaluation (sandbox) — Apr 5–Apr 18
3) Production pilot (limited traffic) — Apr 26–May 24
4) Acceptance & handoff — May 25–May 31

If that looks reasonable I can schedule a 30-minute MAP workshop next week to finalize owners and fill the checklist.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0128

Attachments: MAP_Template_v1.docx

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fabricate.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & evaluation plan for Fabricate pilot

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the doc and the timeline. Initial thoughts: the proposed dates generally work for us; we’re hoping to complete the pilot and procurement by end of May if possible. Our internal owners will be: Nick Patterson (CTO) for technical sign-off, Sara Li (Data Eng) for data ingest, and John Murphy is our procurement lead (jmurphy@fabricate.ai).

Success criteria we care most about:
- Accurate classification / intent detection at scale (we’ll share a few gold sets)
- Throughput: ability to sustain 200 qps with < 500ms p95 (we can be flexible on p99)
- Data handling: we need clear guidance on logging, retention, and redaction; we’ve attached our vendor security questionnaire for the first pass.

Could you also share an example MAP you’ve used with similar customers? The template is helpful, but a filled example would speed internal approvals.

Best,
Olivia
Director, Product Integrations
Fabricate AI

Attachment: Fabricate_Vendor_Sec_Questionnaire.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fabricate.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-10T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & evaluation plan for Fabricate pilot

Olivia —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and for listing the Fabricate owners. I’ve pulled together a short example MAP as slides to illustrate how we typically map milestones, owners, and acceptance criteria (link below). Key updates based on your notes:

- Added a filled example for "Small-scale eval" with sample acceptance criteria and test plan.
- Noted procurement contact and added a procurement milestone in Week 6.
- Marked data handling and SOC2 artifacts as pre-kickoff checklist items.

Proposed evaluation phases (one-paragraph each):
• Discovery (2 weeks): align dataset, success metrics, and security checklist.
• Sandbox eval (2 weeks): ingest 1–3 sample datasets, run quality tests, baseline latency/throughput.
• Pilot (4 weeks): limited traffic (canary) with escalation paths, cost monitoring, and interop tests.
• Acceptance (1 week): handover, runbook, and remediation items.

Slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y2mSAMPLE_EVAL_SLIDES

Monica and Rishi — can you confirm resource availability for a sandbox run April 5–18 and whether we should propose a dedicated test harness for throughput tests?

If Fabricate agrees, I’ll update the MAP doc in Google Drive and circulate the first draft for comment.

- Marcus

Attachments: evaluation-plan-compact.slides

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fabricate.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-12T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & evaluation plan for Fabricate pilot

Everyone —

We can support the sandbox run Apr 5–18. A couple of notes from the CS/ops side:
- We recommend adding a 2-day performance window during the sandbox where we run controlled throughput tests (we can supply a test harness). This will address the 200 qps target and give realistic p95/p99 numbers.
- I’ve attached a short SOC2 summary that should help Fabricate’s security team with the questionnaire. Full artifact bundle available under NDA / procurement.
- Recommend we set a procurement checkpoint on Apr 20: purchase order + contract redlines in DocuSign so procurement can keep the May close target.

Next steps: Marcus, please add the performance window and procurement checkpoint into the MAP document and share the updated link. Olivia — if you can add John Murphy to the Doc so procurement comments land inline, that’ll speed approvals.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Sr Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

- Clarify data deletion and retention timelines in the runbook

Team —

Thanks for the confirmations and the comments in the Doc. I’ve incorporated the procurement checkpoint (Apr 20) and a 2-day performance window during the sandbox into the MAP. Final draft and a downloadable copy are attached: MAP_Template_v1_final.docx. Live doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X8mSAMPLE_MAP_DRAFT (updated).

- Marcus: Schedule 30-minute MAP workshop w/ Fabricate + internal owners (target Mar 23)
